cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Online and social media encompass websites, social networking platforms, blogs, vlogs, wikis, and apps — media products that exist on the internet and often enable audience participation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Websites use conventions: homepage, navigation menu, banner, content sections, hyperlinks, multimedia (images, video, audio), and calls to action.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Social media platforms (Instagram, TikTok, X/Twitter, YouTube, Snapchat) enable user-generated content, social networking, and algorithmic content distribution.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Prosumer culture: audiences are no longer just consumers — they produce, share, and remix content. This democratises media but also creates challenges with misinformation and quality.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Algorithms determine what content users see on social media, based on engagement data. This creates filter bubbles (echo chambers) where users see content that reinforces their views.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Viral content: media that spreads rapidly through sharing on social networks. Virality is driven by emotional appeal, relatability, humour, and shareability rather than quality or importance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Influencers: social media users with large followings who monetise their audience through brand partnerships, advertising, and merchandise. They blur the line between audience and producer.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Participatory culture (Jenkins): fans actively participate in media communities, creating fan fiction, art, videos, and discussions. This gives audiences creative agency but also free labour for media industries.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Data and privacy: online platforms collect user data for targeted advertising and algorithmic personalisation. This raises ethical concerns about surveillance, consent, and manipulation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Online regulation: the Online Safety Act 2023 requires platforms to protect users from harmful content. Ofcom enforces this, but the global nature of the internet makes regulation difficult.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Convergence: smartphones combine multiple media forms (camera, music player, social media, web browser) in one device. This convergence has transformed how audiences consume and produce media.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Online, Social & Participatory Media
cards.back: Digital divide: not everyone has equal access to online media — age, income, location, and disability affect access. This creates inequalities in who can participate in digital culture.

cards.front: What should you know about media studies exam tips — online, social & participatory media?
cards.back: 1. For Online, Social & Participatory Media, use media terminology precisely (e.g. connotation, denotation, representation, ideology) 2. Always analyse how media language creates meaning for specific audiences 3. Reference specific examples from set products to support your analysis 4. When evaluating Online, Social & Participatory Media, consider the role of media industries and cultural contexts 5. For extended answers, debate different interpretations before reaching your own
